title: Distinct components of a Noetherian curve meet in finitely many closed points
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] with topological Krull dimension $\dim Y\le 1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Its irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] form a finite family. For two distinct components $Z_i,Z_j$, every point of $Z_i\cap Z_j$ is closed in $Y$ and the intersection is finite. Consequently the union $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}(Z_i\cap Z_j)$ is a finite set of closed points; if $y\notin T$, it lies on exactly one component.

proof.text: The irreducible components of Y form a finite family by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components].

source.place: Properties Lemma 0BA8, finiteness of irreducible components

proof.text: Fix distinct components $Z_1,Z_2$. If $Z_1\subseteq Z_2$, maximality of $Z_1$ gives equality, a contradiction. Thus the open subset $U=Z_1\setminus Z_2$ of the irreducible subspace $Z_1$ is nonempty. The closed subspace $Z_1$ is sober and T0 by [lem-sc-scheme-sober], Noetherian, and has dimension at most one by the subspace dimension inequality. Apply IsOpen.isClosed_singleton_of_mem_compl from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Topology.KrullDimension, which realizes [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed], to each point of the complement. The closed embedding of $Z_1$ in $Y$ transports its closed singletons to $Y$. No choice of generic points is needed to prove that U is nonempty.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX proof, first paragraph: distinct components have proper intersections and points in them are closed; non-containment follows directly from maximality

proof.text: The already proved source theorem IsOpen.finite_compl_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one, applied to U inside $Z_1$, shows that $Z_1\cap Z_2$ is finite after mapping along the subtype inclusion. Its proof decomposes the closed complement into finitely many irreducible closed subsets by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]; sobriety [lem-sc-scheme-sober] provides their generic points, and [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed] makes these closed, so each piece is a singleton. Thus the separate holed theorem lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite is not needed. Take the finite union over distinct ordered component pairs. Every point belongs to irreducibleComponent y by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. If a point outside T belonged to a different component, that pair of components would witness its membership in T; this gives uniqueness.
